source_title: Quote of the day by Sir Patrick Stewart
source_excerpt: Sir Patrick Stewart was one of the most iconic actors in the Hollywood industry. And as frightening as it may be, pain will make you stronger.âWhat does the quote from Patrick Stewart mean?Patrick Stewart shared these words with his younger self, Charles Xavier, in the 2014 film 'X-Men: Days of Future Past.â In the scene, Wolverine uses his mind as a bridge to allow the older, future Professor X (played by Patrick Stewart) to connect across time and speak directly to his disillusioned 1973 younger self (played by James McAvoy).The statement is all about understanding that struggles, losses, and obstacles do not always define a personâs entire self. He was conveying the emotions to a man who had lost his friends, his school, and his ability to walk and had fallen into a hole of depression and despair. However, human mistake is not human destiny. Failure or complications in life are temporary unless you surrender to the situation and let it all overtake you. Healing and growth are rarely solo journeys; vulnerability is a necessity, and suffering can either paralyze you or serve as a catalyst for growth and resilience, as a lesson that you needed to move forward in life. It argues that vulnerability is not weakness, pain is not an excuse to give up, and no one is beyond saving, including yourself.About Sir Patrick Xavierâs early lifeSir Patrick Stewart was born on July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, in the West Riding of Yorkshire, England. His mother was Gladys (nÃ©e Barrowclough), who used to work as a mill weaver and textile worker, while his father, Alfred George Stewart, was a regimental sergeant major in the British Army who also worked as a general labourer and postman.Stewart led a quiet and struggling lifestyle when he was a young child. His family home lacked some basic amenities since they were living in post-war Yorkshire, and his father suffered from PTSD after his military service. Over the years, the veteran icon had spoken multiple times about the struggles he faced at home and how the stage and acting became his safe place away from everything.While talking to the Guardian in 2009, the actor detailed the domestic violence he faced at home, and from the age of 12 onwards, acting became his escape, especially because he never really liked who he was. He shared at the time, âI managed to find my own refuge in acting. The stage was a far safer place for me than anything I had to live through at homeâit offered escape.âIn another instance, while talking at the 14th Dubai International Film Festival in December 2017, Stewart shared, âOn stage, I was not being Patrick Stewart, of whom I didn't have a particularly high opinion... I was someone else. I so much more enjoyed being someone else than being Patrick Stewart. It's something of a confession, but I have to say: I still feel the same way about what I do.âSir Patrick Xavierâs Hollywood achievement and his legacyHis love for drama began during his school years in Yorkshire, where an encouraging English teacher pushed him to explore reading and performing Shakespeare. By age 12, he had joined a local amateur drama group and memorized Shakespearean speeches for fun. After leaving school by 15, he briefly worked as a journalist, though his commitments to acting and theater did not allow him to continue in the field.Later, he got a grant and scholarship to attend the prestigious Bristol Old Vic Theatre School. During his late teens, he developed alopecia and lost his hair by age 19. His classical training at Bristol laid the groundwork for his eventual work with the Royal Shakespeare Company.Over the course of seven decades, Stewart worked regularly in theater as well as film and TV shows and made a name for himself. He was one of the biggest and most loved stars in the industry. Some of his most remembered roles over the years include the âX-Men Series,' the âStar Trekâ franchise, 'Dune,' 'Excalibur,' âA Christmas Carol,' âRobin Hood: Men in Tights,' âGreen Room,' and many others.Sir Patrick Xavier passed away on October 28 at the age of 86 in his home in Los Angeles.
